1. 북왕국 이스라엘의 멸망의 원인: 1. The causes of the fall of the northern kingdom of Israel
<왕하17:1~6> 유다 왕 아하스 십이년에 엘라의 아들 호세아가 사마리: <2 Kgs 17:1~6> In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years. And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him
- 북왕국의 마지막 왕 호세아가 왕이 되어 또 다시 악을 행했지만 이전: - Hoshea, the last king of the northern kingdom, became king and once again did evil, but not like the kings before him. At this time Shalmaneser V king of Assyria came up and attacked Hoshea, so he paid tribute, then betrayed him and sent messengers to a king of Egypt called ‘So’.
여기 지도 보세요. 고대 앗수르의 영토가 어마어마하죠?: Look at this map here. The territory of ancient Assyria was enormous, wasn't it?
그러니까 살만에셀이 호세아를 가두고 사마리아를 3년을 에워쌉니다. 그리고:
So Shalmaneser locks Hoshea up and besieges Samaria for 3 years. And finally he destroys northern Israel and scatters them among many nations. That was a common tactic in ancient times. So they couldn't even dream of rebelling...And then he swapped them out and planted Assyrian people in Samaria.
 - What caused the fall of the northern kingdom of Israel? It's in verses 7~23, and in a word, it says they didn't keep the Sinai covenant, Leviticus, and that's how they ended up like this.
 - But there's an interesting story in there. Look at verse 25. The Assyrian people who arrived in Samaria didn't serve the LORD, so lions came and killed them. So they reported it to the king of Assyria, and he said, “Bring back a priest and serve the god of that land.” - In other words, serve God.
 - Even the wild beasts are cooperating, and the king of Assyria is cooperating and helping with the mission work, but there are no teachers.
그렇게 앗수르 왕이 보낸 제사장이 가르치긴 했는데 결과는 여호와도 경외하: So the priest the king of Assyria sent did teach them, but the result was that they feared the LORD and also served the gods they had brought with them.
<왕하17:28~33> 이에 사마리아에서 사로잡혀 간 제사장 중 하나가: <2 Kgs 17:28~33> Then one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and lived in Bethel, and taught them how they should fear the LORD. However every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities in which they lived. The men of Babylon made Succoth Benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima, and the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim. So they feared the LORD, and also made from among themselves priests of the high places, who sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places. They feared the LORD, and served their own gods, after the ways of the nations from among whom they had been carried away
세상에 이게 지금 얼마나 좋은 기회예요? 그런데 하나님 말씀을 바르게 가: Good grief, what a great opportunity this was! But since there was no one to teach God's word correctly, this is what happened. That's why here at Hangiseon we do this, to teach all of you, the next generation, the word well
18장 13절 부터 히스기야 와 이야기가 나옵니다.\n - 보통 우리는:
From chapter 18 verse 13 comes the story of Hezekiah.
 - Usually we only remember the good things Hezekiah did. That he prayed and got his life extended. But we have to remember that he had failures as well as achievements. When Assyria invaded he surrendered, and paid the gold and silver the king of Assyria demanded, even stripping what was in the temple.
A talent is about 32 kg, so he was told to bring 10 tons of silver and 1 ton of gold. He brought it so fast that the king thought, “Hey, these guys have a lot of gold,” and just surrounded the whole of Jerusalem. He demands surrender and sends the Rabshakeh, who pours out all kinds of outrageous talk, mocking and blaspheming God.
그제서야 다급해진 히스기야는 이사야에게 사람을 보내는데 이사야를 통해 하: Only then does Hezekiah get desperate and send people to Isaiah, and through Isaiah God tells him he will punish Assyria. He was already going to punish them anyway because of the Rabshakeh's outrageous talk. In the end 185,000 men became corpses in one morning, and Sennacherib went back home and was struck down and killed by his sons.
<왕하20:1> 그 때에 히스기야가 병들어 죽게 되매 아모스의 아들 선지:
<2 Kgs 20:1> In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death. And the prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz came to him, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live
 - Without even knowing they were people headed for ruin, he stripped all the gold off the temple and handed it over, so how could he not get sick?
So God sends Isaiah, and what he says is: you're going to die.
<왕하20:2~3> 히스기야가 낯을 벽으로 향하고 여호와께 기도하여 가로: <2 Kgs 20:2~3> Then he turned his face to the wall, and prayed unto the LORD, saying, I beseech thee, O LORD, remember now how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in thy sight. And Hezekiah wept sore
히스기야가 울고 불고 하면서 젊은 날에 조금 잘한 것을 기억해 달라고 하:
Hezekiah weeps and wails and asks God to remember the few good things he did in his younger days, and God, soft-hearted again just like that, extends his life by 15 years. Even he thought he'd committed a sin worthy of death, so maybe he couldn't believe God would let him live, and he asks for a sign.
 - Shall the shadow of the sun go back 10 degrees? Or go forward? Going forward is easy, so he asks for it to go back.  The earth turned backwards.
 - At this time, Babylon heard that Hezekiah had defeated 185,000 Assyrian soldiers all at once, and sent messengers to make an alliance. But when they found out, it turned out the soldiers had just become corpses overnight. So they quickly switched it to a visit to wish him well in his sickness. And Hezekiah was so moved: “The great empire of Babylon came to visit me in my sickness...” and he showed them everything.
국가 안보시설, 성전 금고부터 시작해서 다 보여 준거야. 이 미친놈이.\:
National security facilities, starting with the temple treasury, he showed them everything. This crazy guy.
 - Then Isaiah rebukes him: ‘All the treasures will be taken away, and your sons will all be dragged off to Babylon and become eunuchs.’ And Hezekiah's answer: ‘As long as there's no trouble in my own lifetime, that's fine.’ Good grief, there's no bigger loser than this.
- 히스기야 죽고 아들 므낫세가 왕이 됨: - Hezekiah dies and his son Manasseh becomes king
<왕하21:1> 므낫세가 위에 나아갈 때에 나이 십이 세라 예루살렘에서: <2 Kgs 21:1> Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hephzibah
엄마 이름 나왔다? 무슨 뜻이라고 했죠? 나쁜 놈이다. 히스기야가 그리: The mother's name is mentioned? What did I say that means? He's a bad one. Hezekiah wasn't such a bad person, but the woman Hephzibah was wicked, so the son turned out that way too. Because of Manasseh's sins, God could not forgive Jerusalem in the end.
<왕하21:11~16> 유다 왕 므낫세가 이 가증한 일과 악을 행함이 그: <2 Kgs 21:11~16> Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations, and has done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, who were before him, and has also made Judah to sin with his idols
<렘15:4> 유다 왕 히스기야의 아들 므낫세가 예루살렘에 행한 바를 인:
<Jer 15:4> I will cause them to be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh the son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for that which he did in Jerusalem
 - So according to tradition, Isaiah, who usually didn't point out the kings' wrongs unless he had to, couldn't stand watching Manasseh's wicked deeds any longer and said something, and Manasseh just had him sawn in two.
 - Manasseh dies and Amon becomes king
 - After that Amon became king, and the officials who couldn't even breathe under Manasseh thought, maybe things will change a little now, but when Amon acted just the same, the officials quietly killed him.
그런데 일반 백성들은 왕을 죽이는 신하가 어디 있냐고 그 신하들을 다시: But the ordinary people said, what kind of officials kill their king? So they killed those officials in turn and made Josiah king.
<왕하22:1~2> 요시야가 위에 나아갈 때에 나이 팔 세라 예루살렘에서:
<2 Kgs 22:1~2> Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty and one years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath. And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in all the way of David his father, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left
 - Even though he became king at 8, after a long time here finally came a king who walked in the way of David and didn't turn aside to the right or the left.
<왕하22:3~11> 요시야 왕 십팔 년에 왕이 므술람의 손자 아살리야의:
<2 Kgs 22:3~11> In the eighteenth year of king Josiah, the king sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, the scribe
- He sent Shaphan to the temple to have it repaired... and Hilkiah the high priest found the scroll of the Law. That's like a cook finding a knife in the kitchen. The priest is supposed to be someone who lives with the Law always on his lips, and he's only finding it for the first time. It was a book thought to be probably Deuteronomy, and when it was taken to king Josiah, he told them to read it.
 -The scribe, reading it for the first time, just read it to king Josiah, who was hearing it for the first time, and yet the king, who was only 26 years old, wept loudly, tore his clothes and repented. Anyway, when king Josiah read the book of the Law, he realized that, not to mention his own father and grandfather,
역대 유대인들이 성경에서 하라고 하는 것은 기를 쓰고 하지 않았고 하지: the Jews through all the generations had stubbornly refused to do what the Bible told them to do, and had risked their lives doing evil, the very things it told them not to do.
얼마나 충격을 먹었던지 남은 생을 전심전력해서 국토 대숙청을 해요. 근데: He was so shocked that he spends the rest of his life with all his heart and strength purging the whole land. But it was too late. Because of Manasseh, God's wrath had already broken out. Even though Josiah carries out a tremendous reform in his own way, God's wrath does not let up.
<왕하23:1~3> 왕이 보내어 유다와 예루살렘의 모든 장로를 자기에게로: <2 Kgs 23:1~3> And the king sent, and they gathered unto him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem. And the king went up into the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people, both small and great: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the LORD. And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant
It says there was no king who did this, before Josiah or after him.
<왕하23:21~24> 왕이 뭇 백성에게 명하여 가로되 이 언약책에 기록: <2 Kgs 23:21~24> And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover unto the LORD your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant. Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah; but in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, wherein this passover was holden to the LORD in Jerusalem. Moreover the workers with familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the images, and the idols, and all the abominations that were spied in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, did Josiah put away, that he might perform the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the LORD
사사시대 이후로 이렇게 유월절을 지킨 사람이 없었다는 것이다. 다윗도,: It means no one had kept the Passover like this since the time of the judges. Not David, not Samuel, not Solomon, nobody kept it.
<왕하23:25~26> 요시야와 같이 마음을 다하며 성품을 다하며 힘을:
<2 Kgs 23:25~26> And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the LORD with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him. Notwithstanding the LORD turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal
 - Even though 20 years had passed since Manasseh died, God's wrath still had not let up. And sadly, a man like this didn't even make it past forty; when the king of Egypt went up to fight Assyria, he meddled for no reason and got himself killed.
이 때 전 백성이 슬퍼했습니다. 그 애통이 얼마나 큰지 나중에 이런 경구:
At this time all the people mourned. Their grief was so great that later a saying came out of it. If someone wept bitterly, people would say, ‘ You're crying like when king Josiah died,’ and that saying became the very byword for grief. Even when it seems like the people know nothing, they all know who the real king is and who's a fake. For one king, it even says he died with no one missing him.
 - When Josiah died, Jehoahaz became king - he did evil. Next came Jehoiakim; Pharaoh Necho changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim.  He paid silver and gold to Pharaoh. Squeezed out of the people...
